sources.title: Primary source 1: https://openai.com/index/inside-our-in-house-data-agent
sources.role: Primary source used for chronology and technical verification

sources.title: Primary source 2: https://openai.com/index/unrolling-the-codex-agent-loop
sources.role: Primary source used for chronology and technical verification

claims.text: OpenAI’s Codex article describes the agent loop as the harness logic orchestrating the user, model inference, tools, conversation history, and context-window management.

OpenAI’s in-house data-agent article describes an internal-only GPT-5.2 agent with layered context (metadata, human annotations, code enrichment, institutional knowledge, memory, runtime context) and pass-through access controls.
The data agent is explicitly an internal tool rather than a public product; examples of faster analysis and improved reliability are OpenAI-reported experience, not an independent benchmark.

limitations.text: The two sources describe different systems and should remain separately attributed even when used as one architecture cluster.
The in-house data-agent lessons are organizational case-study evidence and should not be generalized as a universal architecture benchmark.

Anthropic published Claude’s new constitution on January 22 and states that the document is a crucial part of its model training process that directly shapes Claude behavior.

limitations.text: Cowork was a research preview, so announcement-time product boundaries must not be generalized to later availability.
The constitution describes intended behavior and training guidance; actual model outputs may not always follow its ideals, as Anthropic itself notes.

artifact.canonical_name: Gemini API January 2026 tool and lifecycle updates

sources.title: Primary source 1: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/changelog
sources.role: Primary source used for chronology and technical verification

claims.text: The Gemini API changelog records Computer Use tool support for gemini-3-pro-preview and gemini-3-flash-preview on January 29.
The changelog records a model lifecycle feature on January 12 and support for Cloud Storage/public/private pre-signed database URLs as input sources, with a 100 MB file limit, on January 8.
The changelog also records Veo 4K/portrait-output changes and several alias/deprecation events during January.

limitations.text: Computer Use support is tied to preview model identifiers and must preserve announcement-time preview/deprecation status.
The changelog establishes API availability, not independent quality or safety of computer-use behavior.

sources.title: Primary source 1: https://mistral.ai/news/
sources.role: Primary source used for chronology and technical verification

claims.text: Mistral released Vibe 2.0 on January 27 as a terminal-native coding agent powered by the Devstral 2 model family.
The release added custom subagents, multi-choice clarifications, slash-command skills, unified agent modes, and automatic updates, with availability on Le Chat Pro/Team plus PAYG or BYOK paths.

limitations.text: The announcement is vendor-authored; claims about productivity or model quality are not independently reproduced.
Devstral 2 itself predates January, so the month-level event is the Vibe 2.0 agent/harness update rather than a new underlying model family.
